title: Mary Jackson's birth chart
metaDescription: Mary Jackson's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.3° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 19.3° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Aries, but precisely: 19.3°, second decan, 10°–20°, under the Sun in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Pisces (23.7°), Venus in Taurus (8.9°), Mars in Taurus (11.2°): a mind that absorbs before it argues, taste for the substantial and the lasting, drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Mars square Neptune, 0.2° of separation. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Venus sextile Uranus at 0.9°, and Venus trine Jupiter at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Sun stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Five planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aries at 19.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Pisces at 23.7° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Taurus at 8.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Taurus at 11.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Virgo at 10.0° is in detriment. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 earth, 3 water, 2 fire; by modality, 4 mutable, 3 fixed, 2 cardinal. Earth counts what remains: the built, the kept, the finished. Promise weighs less than delivery. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Venus, Jupiter, Saturn and Neptune were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.4° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
